## 2) Important conceptual nuances

### CI is not just "post-processing"

- Classic post-processing: improve an already interpretable image.
- CI: reconstruct information that is not directly visible in the raw measurement.

### Co-design is central

- Designing optics and algorithms separately is often suboptimal.
- Designing acquisition + reconstruction together allows better noise-resolution-cost compromises.

### The inverse problem is the mathematical heart

- Measurement: partial observation, noisy, often not unique.
- Inference: regularization and prior to choose a physically plausible solution.

---

## 3) Guided mini-cases

### Case A - Night mode smartphone

- Situation: dark scene, small sensor, high noise.
- CI strategy:
  - multi-image acquisition;
  - alignment ;
  - robust fusion;
  - denoising + restoration of details.

### Case B - MA-XRF in heritage

- Situation: superimposed and invisible pigments in RGB.
- CI strategy:
  - spectral acquisition (x, y, energy);
  - spectral deconvolution;
  - elementary cards;
  - physicochemical interpretation.

### Case C - NLOS

- Situation: hidden object out of line of sight.
- CI strategy:
  - pulsed illumination;
  - temporal measurement of rebounds;
  - inversion of light transport.

---

## 4) Active comprehension questions

- Why can optical encoding make the reconstruction more stable?
- In what case is better optics not sufficient without a suitable algorithm?
- Why are CI applications often multi-data?
- How does a prior help an ill-posed problem?

---

## 5) Revision checklist before exam

- I know how to define CI in a precise sentence.
- I know how to explain the difference with traditional imagery.
- I can draw the string encoding -> measurement -> decoding.
- I can cite at least 4 areas of application and their measurement logic.
- I can explain the role of an inverse problem and a prior.

---

## 6) Common mistakes

- Reduce CI to AI only.
- Forget the physical constraints of acquisition.
- Confuse visual improvement and reconstruction of information.
- Ignore compromises (resolution, noise, light, cost, calculation).
